catalog.name: GitLab
catalog.description: Trigger a patrol on a GitLab push, merge request, or issue. Open a merge request with the patrol's result.
catalog.author: Myra

trigger.summary: New push, merge request, or issue matching your rules

config.label: GitLab project
config.description: The project to watch — pick from your GitLab projects, or type a group/project path.

config.label: Event types
config.description: Which GitLab events fire this trigger. Leave empty for all.

auth.label: Sign in
auth.summary: One-click for gitlab.com — nothing to paste. Uses the built-in Myra GitLab app.

auth.label: Token
auth.summary: Paste a personal access token with the "api" scope. Works on any instance.

auth.label: Self-hosted OAuth
auth.summary: Register an OAuth application on your instance ("api" scope), then sign in.

actions.label: Open a merge request
actions.summary: Push the patrol's worktree branch and open it as a draft merge request

config.label: GitLab project
config.description: Pick from your GitLab projects, or type a group/project path.

config.label: Target branch
config.placeholder: Defaults to the project's default branch

config.label: Title
config.description: Leave blank to use the patrol card's title.

config.label: Description
config.description: Leave blank to use the run's result.

config.label: GitLab instance URL
config.description: Only for a self-hosted instance (e.g. https://gitlab.mycompany.com). Leave the default for gitlab.com.

config.label: OAuth application ID
config.description: The built-in Myra GitLab.com app is used by default for one-click Sign in. Override with your own for a self-hosted instance.

config.label: OAuth application secret
config.description: Only for self-hosted OAuth apps. Leave blank for gitlab.com Sign in (PKCE, no secret).

config.label: Poll interval (seconds)
config.description: How often Myra checks GitLab for new merge requests / issues / pushes. 60s is polite; keep >= 30.

config.label: Webhook secret (advanced — instant delivery)
config.description: Optional. Triggers work out of the box by polling — no secret needed. Only set this if you also wire a GitLab webhook for instant (non-polled) delivery; then use the same value as the webhook's "Secret token".
